arxiv-1807-03381.title: New MC determination of the critical coupling in ϕ 2 4 \phi^{4}_{2} theory.
arxiv-1807-03381.creator: Simone Bronzin 1, Barbara De Palma 2, Marco Guagnelli 1,2
arxiv-1807-03381.description: Abstract We investigate the non–perturbative features of ϕ 4 \phi^{4} theory in two dimensions, using Monte Carlo lattice methods. In particular we determine the ratio f 0 ≡ g / μ 2 f_{0}\equiv g/\mu^{2} , where g g is the unrenormalised coupling, in the infinite volume and continuum limit. Our final result is f 0 = 11.

arxiv-2302-03562.title: Flexible Phased Array Sheets: A Techno-Economic Analysis
arxiv-2302-03562.creator: Oren S. Mizrahi, Austin Fikes, Ali Hajimiri
arxiv-2302-03562.description: Abstract Phased arrays have enabled advances in communications, sensing, imaging, and wireless power transfer. In all these applications, large apertures enable higher power, higher data rates, higher resolution, and complex functionalities, but are elusive owing to a correspondingly large cost, mass, and physical size. Flexible phased arrays (FPAs) show potential in breaking this trade-off.

arxiv-2307-12792.title: Deep Homography Prediction for Endoscopic Camera Motion Imitation Learning
arxiv-2307-12792.creator: Martin Huber, Sébastien Ourselin, Christos Bergeles, Tom Vercauteren ⋆
arxiv-2307-12792.description: Abstract In this work, we investigate laparoscopic camera motion automation through imitation learning from retrospective videos of laparoscopic interventions. A novel method is introduced that learns to augment a surgeon’s behavior in image space through object motion invariant image registration via homographies.

arxiv-2312-12963.title: Infinite order results for Charged sectors of the Standard Model
arxiv-2312-12963.creator: Oleg Antipin, Jahmall Bersini, Pantelis Panopoulos, Francesco Sannino, Zhi-Wei Wang
arxiv-2312-12963.description: Abstract We determine anomalous dimensions of a family of fixed hypercharge operators in the Standard Model featuring the general Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa structure. The results are obtained at infinite orders in the couplings and to leading and subleading orders in the charge. The computed anomalous dimensions are shown to agree with the maximum known order in perturbation theory.

arxiv-2402-14806.title: Difference Learning for Air Quality Forecasting Transport Emulation
arxiv-2402-14806.creator: Reed R. Chen, Christopher Ribaudo, Jennifer Sleeman, Chace Ashcraft, Collin Kofroth, Marisa Hughes, Ivanka Stajner, Kevin Viner, Kai Wang
arxiv-2402-14806.description: Abstract Human health is negatively impacted by poor air quality including increased risk for respiratory and cardiovascular disease. Due to a recent increase in extreme air quality events, both globally and locally in the United States, finer resolution air quality forecasting guidance is needed to effectively adapt to these events.

arxiv-2405-05960.title: The effects of bar strength and kinematics on galaxy evolution: slow strong bars affect their hosts the most
arxiv-2405-05960.creator: Tobias Géron, R. J. Smethurst, Chris Lintott, Karen L. Masters, I. L. Garland, Petra Mengistu, David O’Ryan, B.D. Simmons
arxiv-2405-05960.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tobias Géron, R. J. Smethurst, Chris Lintott, Karen L. Masters, I. L. Garland, Petra Mengistu, David O’Ryan, B.D. Simmons. We study how bar strength and bar kinematics affect star formation in different regions of the bar by creating radial profiles of EW[H α \alpha ] and D n 4000 using data from SDSS-IV MaNGA.

arxiv-2503-21091.title: Integrate Meta-analysis into Specific Study (InMASS) for Estimating Conditional Average Treatment Effect
arxiv-2503-21091.creator: Keisuke Hanada, Masahiro Kojima
arxiv-2503-21091.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Keisuke Hanada, Masahiro Kojima. Randomized controlled trials are the standard method for estimating causal effects, ensuring sufficient statistical power and confidence through adequate sample sizes. However, achieving such sample sizes is often challenging. This study proposes a novel method for estimating the average treatment effect (ATE) in a target population by integrating and reconstructing information from previous trials using only summary statistics of outcomes and covariates through meta-analysis. The proposed approach combines meta-analysis, transfer learning, and weighted regression.

arxiv-2504-17880.title: Autonomous Navigation Of Quadrupeds Using Coverage Path Planning
arxiv-2504-17880.creator: Alexander James Becoy, Kseniia Khomenko, Luka Peternel, Raj Thilak Rajan
arxiv-2504-17880.description: Abstract This paper proposes a novel method of coverage path planning for the purpose of scanning an unstructured environment autonomously. The method uses the morphological skeleton of the prior 2D navigation map via SLAM to generate a sequence of points of interest (POIs). This sequence is then ordered to create an optimal path given the robot’s current position.

arxiv-2509-26584.title: Fairness Testing in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: How Small Perturbations Reveal Bias in Small Language Models Conference: Brazilian Symposium on Software Quality; Nov 04–07, 2025; São José dos Campos, SP CCS: Software and its engineering Software verification and validation CCS: Computing methodo
arxiv-2509-26584.creator: Matheus Oliveira, Jonathan Silva (co-advisor) , Awdren Fontão (advisor)
arxiv-2509-26584.description: Abstract . Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely used across multiple domains but continue to raise concerns regarding security and fairness. Beyond known attack vectors such as data poisoning and prompt injection, LLMs are also vulnerable to fairness bugs. These refer to unintended behaviors influenced by sensitive demographic cues (e.g., race or sexual orientation) that should not affect outcomes.

arxiv-2510-26689.title: Stellar Spectroscopy Using Diffraction Grating, CMOS Monochrome Sensor, and Reflecting Telescopes
arxiv-2510-26689.creator: Abhinav Roy, Niti Singh
arxiv-2510-26689.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Abhinav Roy, Niti Singh. We present the design and testing of a compact, low-cost stellar spectrometer developed for undergraduate and outreach applications. The instrument employs a 600 lines/mm diffraction grating, a CMOS monochrome sensor, and a 3D-printed mount integrated with reflecting telescopes. Calibration was performed using helium emission sources in the laboratory and Vega as a spectrophotometric standard, supported by a custom Python-based image-processing pipeline for wavelength calibration and spectral stacking.

pmc-10580950.title: Novel mechanism of hydrogen peroxide for promoting efficient natamycin synthesis in Streptomyces
pmc-10580950.creator: Gongli Zong, Guangxiang Cao, Jiafang Fu, Peipei Zhang, Xi Chen, Wenxiu Yan, Lulu Xin, Zhongxue Wang, Yan Xu, Rongzhen Zhang
pmc-10580950.description: The mechanism of regulation of natamycin biosynthesis by Streptomyces in response to oxidative stress is unclear. Here, we first show cholesterol oxidase SgnE, which catalyzes the formation of H2O2 from sterols, triggered a series of redox-dependent interactions to stimulate natamycin production in S. gilvosporeus.

pmc-10599035.title: Characteristics of sodium and water retention in rats with nephrotic syndrome induced by puromycin aminonucleoside
pmc-10599035.creator: Zaiping Xu, Yunlai Wang, Ye Feng, Mo Yang, Gaoxiang Shi, Zihua Xuan, Fan Xu
pmc-10599035.description: IntroductionNephrotic syndrome (NS) is characterized by renal sodium and water retention. The mechanisms are not fully elucidated.MethodsThe NS rat model was established by single intraperitoneal injection of 100 mg/kg puromycin aminonucleoside (PAN). The plasma electrolyte level and urinary sodium excretion were monitored dynamically.

pmc-11446693.title: Myosteatosis and muscle loss impact liver transplant outcomes in male patients with hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-11446693.creator: Di Lu, Zhihang Hu, Hao Chen, Abid Ali Khan, Qingguo Xu, Zuyuan Lin, Huigang Li, Jianyong Zhuo, Chiyu He, Li Zhuang, Zhe Yang, Siyi Dong, Jinzhen Cai, Shusen Zheng, Xiao Xu
pmc-11446693.description: BackgroundSarcopenia is associated with unfavourable long‐term survival in patients undergoing liver transplantation (LT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, the impact of myosteatosis and muscle loss on patient prognosis has not been investigated.MethodsSeven hundred fifty‐six HCC patients who received LT at 3 transplant centres were included.

pmc-11534105.title: Real-world effectiveness of first- and second-line anti-angiogenesis therapy in RCC: analysis of a UK-based population
pmc-11534105.creator: Tom Waddell, Manon Pillai, Kate Armitage, Donna M Graham, Michael Moran, Maria Dilleen, Sinead Holmes, Ewa Śleszyńska-Dopiera, Robert Hawkins
pmc-11534105.description: Aim: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the seventh commonest cancer in the UK, where first-line (1L) sunitinib and second-line (2L) axitinib are treatment options.Methods: Retrospective, non-interventional data from the Christie NHS Foundation Trust (Manchester, UK). The primary end point was median progression-free survival (mPFS).

pmc-12429125.title: Redox Status in Patients Suffering from Multiple Chemical Sensitivity (MCS): A Pilot Study
pmc-12429125.creator: Paula Aranda-Martínez, Nerea Menéndez-Coto, Ana Coto-Montes, María Martín-Estebané, Germaine Escames, Darío Acuña-Castroviejo, Takao Fujisawa
pmc-12429125.description: Background/Objectives: Multiple chemical sensitivity (MCS) is a complex environmental illness characterized by intolerance to various environmental chemicals, affecting multiple organ systems. Despite its prevalence, MCS remains poorly understood, with limited recognition by the World Health Organisation amid challenges in diagnosis due to symptom heterogeneity.

pmc-12568132.title: Strain and Sex Variability in Liver, Kidney and Lung Levels of DNA Adducts EB-GII and bis-N7G-BD Following Inhalation Exposure to 1,3-Butadiene in Collaborative Cross Mice
pmc-12568132.creator: Erik Moran, Samantha Goodman, Fred A Wright, Richard Evans, Natalia Y Tretyakova, Ivan Rusyn, Małgorzata Dobrzyńska
pmc-12568132.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). 1,3-butadiene (BD) is a volatile organic pollutant. Upon inhalation, it is metabolically activated to reactive epoxides which alkylate genomic DNA and form potentially mutagenic monoadducts and DNA–DNA crosslinks including N7-(1-hydroxyl-3-buten-1-yl)guanine (EB-GII) and 1,4-bis-(guan-7-yl)-2,3-butanediol (bis-N7G-BD). While metabolic activation resulting in mutagenicity is a well-established mode of action for 1,3-butadiene, characterization of the extent of inter-individual variability in response to BD exposure is a gap in our knowledge.

pmc-12655380.title: Vitamin D Status as a Late Pregnancy Biomarker of Perceived Stress
pmc-12655380.creator: Maya F Andrade, Anjali G Borsum, Mathew J Gregoski, Myla D Ebeling, Judith R Shary, Martin Hewison, Bruce W Hollis, Carol L Wagner
pmc-12655380.description: Background/Objectives: Stress during pregnancy critically impacts maternal and fetal health. While prior research has linked sociodemographic and biological factors to stress levels, the role of specific biomarkers, such as vitamin D (VD), remains unexplored. This study examined the relationships among sociodemographic factors, VD status (as measured by serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentration), and perceived stress in pregnant women.

pmc-12775051.title: Automated identification of Shankha Prakshalana yoga poses with machine learning techniques
pmc-12775051.creator: Abhishek Sharma, Vaidehi Sharma, Premansh Sharma, Rishikesh Ladha, Yogesh Lamba, Sulabh Bansal
pmc-12775051.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This research presents an innovative model for automatically detecting yoga poses, specifically focusing on the yogic kriya known as “Shankha Prakshalana.” The proposed system utilizes advanced computer vision techniques to extract pose features from yoga videos for classification purposes. A carefully annotated dataset comprising videos of individuals practicing Shankha Prakshalana was used to train and evaluate various machine learning (ML) architectures, incorporating both supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms.

pmc-12817814.title: Metformin and its derivatives in breast cancer: from glycaemic control to tumor-intrinsic pathways
pmc-12817814.creator: Rohina Alim, Hewa Marambage Kasuni Akalanka
pmc-12817814.description: BackgroundBreast cancer (BC) remains the most commonly diagnosed malignancy among women worldwide, with metabolic dysregulation of glucose and hyperinsulinemia increasingly recognised as contributors to its development and progression. However, despite accumulating evidence linking metabolic imbalances to tumorigenesis, the precise therapeutic opportunities arising from targeting these metabolic pathways remain insufficiently defined.

pmc-13028439.title: Thyroidectomy-Related Dysphagia: A Systematic Literature Review
pmc-13028439.creator: Eleni Litsou, Chrissa Sioka, Konstantinos Mpakogiannis, Labrini Magou, Polyxeni Fakitsa, Alexandros Giannakis, Sakkou Sissy Foteini, Fotios Fousekis
pmc-13028439.description: Background and Objectives: Dysphagia is a frequently reported symptom among patients undergoing thyroidectomy, yet its incidence, underlying mechanisms, and temporal progression remain insufficiently clarified. The aim of the present systematic review was to synthesize the existing literature on the occurrence and evolution of swallowing disorders following thyroidectomy, without restriction regarding the extent of surgery, surgical approach, indication, or concomitant complications.

pmc-13188463.title: Mechanistic insights and ameliorative strategies: advances in DEHP-induced metabolic toxicity and intervention by natural bioactive compounds and probiotics
pmc-13188463.creator: Huanyu Cui, Yansong Hu, Ye Tang, Tingzhuang Yi, Shengkui Tan, Zhengbao Zhang, Xiaonian Zhu
pmc-13188463.description: Di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is a ubiquitous plasticizer and environmental contaminant linked to severe metabolic disorders. This review concisely elucidates the multi-organ mechanisms of DEHP-induced toxicity, highlighting its disruption of lipid, glucose, and protein homeostasis. Specifically, we delineate the crucial crosstalk between oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and inflammatory pathways that drive DEHP pathobiology.

pmc-13261052.title: Influenza coinfection inhibits control of mycobacterial infection in a human challenge model
pmc-13261052.creator: Claire M Broderick, Oliver Powell, Sam Nichols, Giselle D’Souza, Dominic Habgood-Coote, Carlota Miranda-Sole, Emily M Whettlock, Zoe Gardener, Emma Bergstrom, Victoria J Wright, Christopher W Woods, Christopher Chiu, Sandra M Newton, Elizabeth Whittaker, Michael Levin, Myrsini Kaforou

pmc-13267560.title: Developing a pan cancer therapy based on DISE-inducing short RNAs
pmc-13267560.creator: Andrea E. Murmann, Mehrnoosh Ebadi, Monal Patel, Alexander Ewe, Sergio Barajas, Shiyu Xiao, Min Jun Ko, Sanghee Lee, Wenjie Cai, Bidur Paudel, Limin Sun, Elizabeth T. Bartom, Masha Kocherginsky, Yan Liu, Dong-Hyun Kim, Achim Aigner, Marcus E. Peter
pmc-13267560.description: RNA interference (RNAi) regulates gene expression through small RNAs that act via Argonaute-containing RNA-induced silencing complexes (RISCs). We previously found that short RNAs with G-rich 6mer seeds (e.g., GGGGGC and G5C) can kill cells by targeting C-rich 3′ UTR seed matches in essential survival genes (SGs), a mechanism termed death induced by survival gene elimination (DISE).

pmc-13320045.title: Driving the future of geriatric and musculoskeletal medicine—the continuing ascent of ACER

pmc-13386782.title: Whole genome sequencing in oesophageal adenocarcinoma unmasks potential precision therapies
pmc-13386782.creator: Sowmya Sharma, Ho Yi Wong, Rebecca L Johnston, Lambros T Koufariotis, Scott Wood, Georgina Hollway, Lauren G Aoude, Aimee L Davidson, John V Pearson, Frank P Lin, Andrew P Barbour, Nicola Waddell
pmc-13386782.description: BackgroundOesophageal adenocarcinoma (OAC) incidence continues to rise in developed countries.
